battle.name: 唐平劉稹澤潞之戰
battle.brief: 會昌三年五月，昭義軍節度使劉悟病歿，軍中越詔立其子劉稹自為留後，朝廷分道出師討之，久攻潞州城不下，終於會昌四年春罷兵招撫。卡面以羅馬重步兵作對照：唐代重裝步卒同樣以鎧盾結陣、弩箭壓制，兩者皆靠嚴整陣列與補給線撐住戰線。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 交戰一方是唐中央朝廷及其徵發的藩鎮聯軍。會昌三年五月，昭義軍節度使劉悟病歿，軍中越過朝廷自行推舉其子劉稹自為留後；中央詔令其聽候處置，劉稹不受詔，朝廷自此視昭義軍為叛鎮。唐廷的出兵體系仍沿用中唐以來的藩鎮兵制：河東節度使劉崇諒領河東軍為北面主力，河中自蒲州出師策應，河北的成德、魏博諸道奉詔出兵，東路直指澤州；總攬戰略的是同平章事李德裕，各道將領各統本部兵馬，朝廷另遣監軍、詔使隨軍監臨，度支與轉運判官在後方籌糧。另一方是昭義軍節度使劉稹所領的潞州、澤州兩州軍鎮，兵權由劉悟一門父子相傳，州兵、縣兵與牙兵編制各有所屬，糧餉自本鎮財賦中自給，名義上仍奉唐正朔，實際上自置官吏、徵收租稅，並控制太行山南北的通道。兩軍同屬唐廷麾下的藩鎮兵，卻分屬兩個互不節制的系統，故此役自開戰起便帶有朝廷內戰的性質。
countriesEn: One side in this conflict was the Tang central court together with the armies it mustered from the circuits. In the fifth month of the third year of Huichang (843) Liu Wu, military governor of Zhaoyi, died of illness, and his own command installed his son Liu Zhen as acting governor without waiting for the court's orders. The court issued edicts telling Liu Zhen to await further instructions; Liu Zhen would not accept them, and from that point the court treated Zhaoyi as a rebel circuit. The Tang war effort still ran on the circuit system of the middle Tang: Liu Chongliang, governor of Hedong, led the Hedong army as the northern main force; Hezhong marched out from Puzhou to support them; and the Hebei circuits of Chengde and Weibo sent troops in response to edict, pressing the eastern approach to Zhaozhou. The overall direction of the campaign rested with the chancellor Li Deyu, who held the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs; each circuit commander led his own men, the court attached supervisors and envoys to watch the army in the field, and the Board of Works and the transport officials raised provisions behind the lines. The other side was the Zhaoyi army of Liu Zhen, covering the two prefectures of Lu and Ze. Command there had passed from father to son inside the Liu family; prefectural, county and elite guard troops were each bound to their own formations, and the circuit paid for itself from the taxes it kept back. It still nominally served the Tang ruler and calendar, while in practice appointing its own officials, collecting its own revenues and holding the passes of the Taihang range. Both armies were circuit armies of the same dynasty, yet they belonged to two systems that answered to no common commander, so the war was in its nature a civil war inside the Tang state.
people: 昭義軍方面，劉悟是前任節度使，鎮上黨十餘年，會昌三年五月病歿；其子劉稹在軍中擁護下自為留後，拒絕朝廷詔令，成為這場衝突的核心人物。劉稹的幕僚與部將分守潞州城與澤州晉城，並向河北、河東各鎮遣使遊說，試圖孤立朝廷。朝廷一方，會昌年間在位的是武宗，樞密與戰略出自同平章事李德裕之手，他堅持用兵，理由是昭義軍據上黨逼近河東，若不示以威懾，河東與河北諸藩將人人觀望，中央威令將盡失；河東節度使劉崇諒奉詔為北面統帥，諸道兵將多不屬於他，籌糧之責也落在河東與河中兩處。沙陀部的李克用其時在河東軍中效力，隨軍出戰，以驍騎見長，是此役後來聲名鵲起的一支力量。同一時期朝中宰相與宦官勢力對用兵與和議各有所圖，議和之說先已隱現於幕間。現存史籍對將佐姓名、斬獲數目記載極為疏略，諸說並存，難以一一坐實。
peopleEn: On the Zhaoyi side, Liu Wu was the outgoing military governor, who had held Shangdang for more than a decade; he died of illness in the fifth month of the third year of Huichang, and under the support of his own command his son Liu Zhen took himself as acting governor, refused the court's edicts and became the central figure of the conflict. Liu Zhen's staff and division commanders defended the city of Lu and the city of Ze in Zhaozhou, and sent envoys to the circuits of Hedong and Hebei to argue that the court was light on its oaths and kept the war too long, hoping to isolate the central government. On the court's side, the emperor in the years of Huichang was Wu Zong, but the direction of the war lay with Li Deyu, chancellor and keeper of the Bureau of Military Affairs, who insisted on going to war. His reasoning was that Zhaoyi, sitting on Shangdang, pressed against Hedong; if Liu Zhen were tolerated, every circuit in Hedong and Hebei would sit and wait, and the authority of the centre would be lost entirely. Liu Chongliang, governor of Hedong, was given command of the northern front, yet the commanders of the various circuits would not submit to him, and the burden of feeding the army fell on Hedong and Hezhong. Li Keyong, of the Shatuo, was then serving in the Hedong army and campaigned with it, his light horse being one of the forces that would make his name later on. At the same time the struggle between chancellors and eunuchs in the capital shaped both the case for war and the case for negotiation, and talk of peace had already begun to surface behind the scenes. The surviving records are extremely thin on the names of subordinates and on casualty figures, several versions circulate side by side, and nothing here can be pinned down with certainty.
kits: 卡面所繪是羅馬重步兵（Legionary）：公元前一世紀以後帝國軍的核心，分段鎧甲（lorica segmentata）綴於肩帶與腰帶之上，大盾（scutum）護住左側，配短柄直劍（gladius）與標槍（pilum），靠整列持盾前進、投射標槍而後近身搏鬥的固定動作作戰。這個兵種並不出現在八四三年的上黨戰場，作為跨時空的對照，它說明的是重裝步卒的通用樣板：結陣、以盾抵矢、以近戰兵器定勝敗，而非靠單兵武藝。至於唐代昭義軍與朝廷聯軍那邊，實際裝備是步卒著明光鎧、鎲甲與兜鍪，配長形或橢圓形步盾，射手用弩與弓箭，步兵以唐刀、陌刀與長矛（槊）應敵；騎兵有馬鎧、馬鐙與長槊，河北與河東諸道騎兵數量可觀，昭義軍據太行陘口亦便於輕騎出入。攻城方面，朝廷據一類官書調集雲梯、飛樓、木牛、撞竿、投石機（發石機）與攻城器械，昭義軍則備礮石、拒馬、鹿角與加築之壘。通信與後勤靠旌節、牙旗、鼓吹、鈞天樂、令旗與烽燧，軍糧自河中、太原沿黃河與汾水轉運，以車、馬、舟並行；藥材、鐵料、弓弦與箭桿多在沿途州縣就地徵發。羅馬重步兵靠補充兵源與補給線維持，昭義軍靠本鎮財賦，唐廷靠轉運，三者的強弱在這場戰役裡恰好可以互相比照。
kitsEn: The card shows a Roman legionary: the core of the imperial army from the first century BC onward, wearing segmented plate armour (lorica segmentata) hung from shoulder and waist belts, carrying a large oval shield (scutum) on the left, and armed with a short thrusting sword (gladius) and the javelin (pilum); his fighting was a fixed drill of advancing in line behind shields, hurling javelins and then closing to hand-to-hand combat. This troop never appeared on the field at Shangdang in 843, and taken as a comparison across eras it shows the general template of the heavy infantryman: formation, shields against arrows, and close combat to decide the issue, not individual swordsmanship. On the Tang side the actual kit of the Zhaoyi and allied court troops was different: foot soldiers wore brigandine (mingguang jia), plated mail and iron helmets, and carried long or oval shields; shooters used bows and crossbows; infantry fought with Tang sabres, miodao and long spears; the cavalry had caparisoned horses, stirrups and long spears, and the mounted contingents of the Hebei and Hedong circuits were considerable, while Zhaoyi's position astride the Taihang passes suited light horse movements. For the siege the court, drawing on official manuals, assembled scaling ladders, siege towers, wooden oxen, battering poles, traction trebuchets and assault equipment, while Zhaoyi had stones, chevaux-de-frise, spiked barriers and reinforced earthworks. Command and supply ran on banners and tally-sticks, war flags, drums and pipes, the music of the Juntian, command flags and beacon fires, and the grain was moved from Hezhong and Taiyuan by cart, horse and barge along the Yellow River and the Fen; medicines, iron, bowstrings and arrow shafts were requisitioned from the prefectures and counties along the way. The Roman legionary stayed strong through the supply of fresh recruits and lines of supply; Zhaoyi paid for itself out of its own circuit revenues; the court depended on transport. Those three systems of strength can be set side by side in this campaign.
tactics: 昭義軍的處置是典型的守城待援：依上黨山岡築壘，閉門不出，絕不出城與官軍決戰，官軍逼近則退守城圈，官軍遠則遣輕騎掠擾糧道；同時堅壁清野，使唐軍無糧可掠，又分兵據澤州晉城與各縣，斷絕東路，並遣使遊說河東、河北諸藩，指朝廷薄於盟誓、兵久不還，意在使朝廷腹背受敵。唐軍的戰法則是多路合擊、逐步壓縮：河東軍自東北沿太行諸陘南下，河中軍自西面渡黃河策應，河北諸道兵出井陘方向威脅澤州，形成對上黨的包抄；前鋒結壘逼近城下，外圍築壘塹、造飛梯雲梯、穴地進兵，並驅使降卒先登，試圖以器械破城；中軍設於後方，護著糧隊與器械營，騎兵則繞行以斷敵援。戰局卻膠著在攻城與運糧兩點：攻城器械損耗、穴地進度緩慢，糧隊自河中陸運數百里，車馬疲敝，遇上冬令霜雪與疫病，將士病者增多，兵氣漸餒；各道兵又互不統屬，賞罰不一，前鋒與後隊屢有爭功推過。兩年之間，唐軍未能破城，昭義軍也未能合兵出擊，戰局始終維持在僵持狀態。
tacticsEn: Zhaoyi's answer was to hold the city and wait for relief. It built its position on the heights of Shangdang, kept the gates shut, refused to risk a field battle, withdrew into the circuit when the imperial army came close and sent light horse to harry the supply line when it pulled back. At the same time it stripped the countryside so the imperial army could find nothing to seize, held Zhaozhou and the counties with separate detachments to cut the eastern road, and sent envoys to the neighbouring circuits to argue that the court was light on its oaths and kept the war too long, hoping to leave the central government with enemies on two sides. The Tang plan was convergence from several quarters with a steady tightening of the noose: the Hedong army came down from the north-east along the Taihang passes, the Hezhong army crossed the Yellow River from the west, and troops from Hebei came out by the Jingxing route to threaten Zhaozhou, so that Shangdang would be surrounded. The vanguard fenced in a camp and pressed up to the walls, raising earthworks and trenches, building ladders and towers, driving mines under the defences and putting surrendered men up the walls first, in the attempt to break the city with engines; the central camp stood well back, guarding the baggage train and the engine park, while cavalry rode round to cut the enemy's relief. The deadlock, however, lay in two things: the siege engines wore out and the mining advanced slowly, and the grain teams had to haul supplies several hundred li inland from Hezhong with carts and horses exhausted, while winter frost and snow and then sickness thinned the ranks and sapped the mood of the soldiers. The troops of the different circuits were also beyond common command, rewards and punishments differed, and the vanguard and the rear columns repeatedly quarrelled over credit and blame. Between one year and the next the Tang army never took the city, and Zhaoyi never came out in force; the match stayed frozen.
data: 可確認的數字有限，須以概略記之。時間上，自會昌三年五月劉悟病歿、六月劉稹不受詔、七月朝廷下詔討伐，到會昌四年春下詔罷兵，前後約十個月，其中真正圍城的時段不過數月。地理上，潞州城即今山西長治一帶，據高岡而築，四面坡陡；昭義軍所據的澤州晉城在其東南，兩州相隔約百餘里。北面主力河東軍由太原南下，行程約五百餘里；西面河中由蒲州運糧，前線距蒲州亦數百里。兵員方面，河東、河中、河北諸道出動之兵合計當以數萬計，昭義軍自有州兵、縣兵與牙兵，總數亦以萬計，雙方確數均不傳於史。糧秣方面，轉運的米粟常被形容為數十萬石之巨，度支為此屢次告急，而運價與民夫之費又倍之。消耗方面，將士多死於疲病、疫癘與飢餓，加上攻城器械的折損與走失，至罷兵時兩軍士氣俱疲；至於斬獲、被擄與攻城之戰的具體數目，現存史籍多略而不詳，諸說並存，寧缺毋濫。
dataEn: The figures that can be confirmed are few and have to be given loosely. In time, from Liu Wu's death in the fifth month of the third year of Huichang, and Liu Zhen's refusal of the edicts in the sixth month, and the court's order to punish him in the seventh, down to the edict recalling the army in the spring of the fourth year of Huichang, the whole business ran about ten months, of which the actual siege covered only a few months. In geography, the city of Lu corresponds to the area of present-day Changzhi in Shanxi, built on a high ridge with steep slopes on every side, and the city of Jincheng in Zhaozhou, which Zhaoyi held, lay about a hundred li to its south-east, the two prefectures being roughly that far apart. The northern main force came down from Taiyuan, a run of about five hundred li, and on the western side provisions were carried from Puzhou, itself several hundred li from the front. In numbers of men, the contingents of Hedong, Hezhong and Hebei together must have amounted to tens of thousands, and Zhaoyi had prefectural, county and guard troops of its own, likewise counted in tens of thousands; the exact totals are not transmitted in the histories. In provisions, the grain moved is commonly described as reaching hundreds of thousands of bushels, and the Board of Works repeatedly reported that it was running short, while the cost of transport and the labour of the corvée came on top of that. In losses, soldiers died in the main of exhaustion, sickness and hunger, added to the breakage and loss of siege engines, and by the time the army was withdrawn both sides were worn out; as for the counts of killed, captured and taken in the assaults, the surviving records are mostly silent and versions differ, so it is better to leave them out than to invent them.
cause: 直接起因是昭義軍的父子相繼與中央對藩鎮兵權的僵持。劉悟鎮昭義軍多年，節度使、觀察使、檢校官銜雖由朝廷頒下，地方軍政財權卻盡歸其手，州縣官吏由他署置，賦稅留於本鎮，這是唐中葉藩鎮的通例，也是昭義軍自恃的根柢。劉悟一死，軍中依慣例推劉稹自為留後，中央不願就此承認一位自行接位的節度使，詔令其聽候朝廷另行安排；劉稹既不交出兵權，也不肯奉詔，這一僵持把藩鎮慣例與朝廷命令直接頂了起來，遂成刀兵之禍。朝廷之所以用兵，李德裕的籌劃最見分明：昭義據上黨，界連河東、河北，若容忍劉稹自據，諸藩便人人觀望，中央再無號召之力；同時會昌以來軍費稍整、兩稅與鹽榷之入粗有可支，若不一舉示懲，恐其勢愈固。此外北邊契丹與吐蕃的壓力仍在，唐廷不宜把兵力長久耗在一州一鎮之上，於是用兵既為取信於天下，也是兩害相權之計。以河東為北面主力，實因昭義正扼太行要道，捨河東則師出無功；河北諸道受命策應，是為斷其東援、接應澤州方向；而劉稹之所以敢拒詔，則在於他自恃上黨地險城堅、糧儲可支，又看準朝廷用兵久必生變。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the succession of the Liu family and a deadlock between the centre and the circuit over military power. Liu Wu had governed Zhaoyi for many years; the titles of military governor, commissioner and honorary offices were bestowed by the court, but the civil, military and fiscal powers of the circuit remained entirely with him, county officials were appointed by him and the revenues stayed in the circuit. That was the normal arrangement of circuits in the middle Tang and also the root of Zhaoyi's self-confidence. When Liu Wu died, his command followed custom and set up Liu Zhen as acting governor; the court would not simply accept a governor who had taken his own seat, and ordered him to wait for the court's own arrangement. Liu Zhen neither handed over his troops nor accepted the edicts, and this standoff drove the routine of the circuit directly against the command of the throne, which is how it came to blows. As for why the court went to war, the plan of Li Deyu is the clearest statement of it: Zhaoyi sat on Shangdang and touched Hedong and Hebei; if Liu Zhen were tolerated, every circuit would look on and wait, and the centre would have no power to summon anyone. Meanwhile, since the years of Huichang the state's revenue had been put into some order, the two-tax and the salt monopoly yielding something to spend, and if the court did not punish this one case the separatist power there would only harden. Pressure from the Khitan and the Tibetans to the north was real as well, and the court could not tie up its forces at one prefecture for long, so the war was meant both to win the allegiance of the realm and to choose the lesser of two harms. Hedong was chosen as the northern main force precisely because Zhaoyi gripped the vital passes of the Taihang; without Hedong no army could reach the front at all. Hebei was ordered to act in concert in order to cut off eastern relief and to support the Zhaozhou flank. And Liu Zhen dared to refuse the edicts because he counted on the terrain and the strength of the city of Shangdang, on provisions that would hold for months, and on the fact that a war of this kind always wore the court out sooner or later.
impact: 此役最直接的結果，是問題被推遲而非解決：劉稹保住了昭義軍節度使的名位與潞、澤兩州的實權，唐廷則以一次沒有勝利的退兵換取了表面的服從。從此，中央與昭義的角力轉入漫長的消耗，宣宗、懿宗先後嘗試分割昭義、增置監軍、徵召藩鎮子弟入宿衛與限制牙兵，都要一點一點地削，無一奏效。劉稹於大中二年（一八四八年）死後，昭義軍內部迅速陷入爭嗣與驕兵的混亂，節度使頻頻更替而朝廷處置愈難，昭義軍逐漸由一個完整的藩鎮變成各方窺伺的缺口。到了唐末，澤州、潞州相繼為河東沙陀李氏所收，昭義軍之名存而實亡，山西北部盡歸河東節度使節制，而李克用父子正是靠河東兵馬與昭義地盤坐大，最終承接大唐的殘局。於長時段而言，此役還留下兩個教訓：其一，朝廷對藩鎮的戰爭往往曠日持久，糧運與軍心才是真正決定勝負的東西，攻城器械再多也難破一座自守之堅城；其二，削藩若不能配合經濟與人事上的釜底抽薪，單憑一次會戰便難以扭轉割據的格局。反觀個人，劉稹的結局亦有餘味：他拒詔而起，卻得節度使之名而終老其位；據說其子劉仁恭後來成了幽州節度使，父子兩代與幽州、河東兩處強藩的緣分，成了一段耐人尋味的支線。
impactEn: The most direct effect of the campaign was that the problem was postponed rather than solved: Liu Zhen kept the title of military governor of Zhaoyi and the real power over Lu and Ze, and the Tang court bought a show of obedience with a withdrawal that won nothing. From then on the struggle between the centre and Zhaoyi settled into a long grind. Xuanzong and Yizong in turn tried to split the circuit, add supervisors, summon the sons of the circuit governors to the capital and restrict the guard troops, all of it done a little at a time and none of it working. After Liu Zhen died in the second year of Dazhong (848), Zhaoyi fell quickly into quarrels over the succession and mutinous troops; its governors changed hands again and again while the court found it harder and harder to manage, and what had been a complete circuit became a gap for every side to covet. By the end of the Tang, Ze and Lu passed in turn to the Shatuo Li of Hedong, the name of Zhaoyi survived while its substance withered, and all of northern Shanxi came under the Hedong governor. The Li Keyong father and son built their strength on the Hedong soldiers and on the Zhaoyi lands, and they were the ones who inherited the remains of the Tang. In the longer run the campaign left two lessons. First, wars by the court against circuits tend to be drawn out, and it is supply and army morale, not the number of siege engines, that decides them; a self-sufficient walled city cannot be taken by engines alone. Second, reducing the circuits without working at the same time on the financial and personnel side cannot turn the pattern around: a single campaign could not undo decades of separatism. Looking back at the man himself there is something to note: Liu Zhen rebelled and yet died in office as military governor of Zhaoyi; it is said that his son Liu Jingong later became military governor of Youzhou, so that two successive generations were bound in one way or another to the two strong circuits of Youzhou and Hedong, which is a curious thread in the story.

resultEn: The war ended with the court recalling its troops. In the spring of the fourth year of Huichang the edict withdrew the army and ended the punitive expedition, appointed Liu Zhen military governor of Zhaoyi, and left him in command of Lu and Ze with his military, civil and fiscal powers untouched; Liu Zhen sent an envoy to tender an apology and offer tribute, the court answered with a gracious edict of comfort, and each side got what it wanted. From then on Zhaoyi was formally back within the Tang's registers while remaining in practice self-governed, the court's effort to reduce it was brought to a close, and Liu Zhen sat stably in that post for several years until he died of illness in the second year of Dazhong. For the Tang court this was a typical failure by retreat: the armies of Hedong, Hezhong and Hebei marched out and came home having achieved nothing, the Board of Works spent a great deal on transport, the soldiers were worn out by the roads and the siege engines, and in exchange they got a city still governed by Liu Zhen. For Zhaoyi the defensive victory was real, but it handed the next generation the same unsolved problem: after Liu Zhen died there was no strong master in the circuit, the court's interference grew more frequent, and only at the end of the Tang, when Ze and Lu passed to Hedong, did the name of Zhaoyi disappear with them. Historians who write of this campaign generally put the point not in the gain or loss of one city, but in the court's financial and transport capacity on the one hand and the resilience of the circuit's own organisation on the other: the first was not enough to sustain a long siege, the second was enough to sustain a long resistance, and once the two stood opposed the result was a stalemate decided long before the army marched out.
